title: New elevator handed over after heavy finishing: why the previous counterweight calculation no longer applies
description: When a permanent cabin mass is added, the unchanged rated load does not preserve the balancing coefficient. Conditional calculation: 0.4 versus 0.2.
seo_title: Heavy finishing of a new elevator: cabin mass and counterweight calculation
seo_description: The cabin rated at 1000 kg received 200 kg of finishing, while the counterweight of 1400 kg and the load of 1000 kg remained unchanged. We examine the change in the coefficient from 0.4 to 0.2 and the error of the old calculation upon handover.
seo_keywords: elevator finishing cabin mass, balancing coefficient counterweight, new elevator handover configuration calculation
content:
The documents for the new elevator must relate to the cabin in the configuration actually being handed over. If heavy finishing was added after the balancing calculation, the previous empty cabin mass may become an incorrect baseline value. In the conditional example, with an unchanged counterweight, the balancing coefficient decreases from 0.4 to 0.2. The old positive calculation does not describe the installed configuration.

What changed before handover of the building

The developer hands over traction elevator L-10. The relevant calculation model uses three masses: P — empty cabin in full intended composition, Q — nominal useful load, W — counterweight. For a separate balancing check, the ratio W = P + qQ is set. The value q shows what fraction of the nominal useful load is added to the empty cabin mass when determining the counterweight.

According to the conditions of the учебный project, q = 0.4 is required. In the original calculation, P is 1000 kg, Q is 1000 kg, W is 1400 kg. All values relate to the same intended model boundaries; additional influences that could change its applicability are considered in the source materials. No full traction or brake calculation of the elevator is built here.

Then, before commissioning, 200 kg of finishing was added. In the example, it is reliably established that this is a new permanent mass of the cabin, not previously accounted for in P. The counterweight mass and nominal useful load remained unchanged. The supplier included the original calculation and referred to the unchanged "1000 kg" label as proof of absence of changes.

Recalculation shows a definite discrepancy

First, let us verify the previous result: q = (W − P) / Q = (1400 − 1000) / 1000 = 0.4. It correctly described the original configuration. The number 0.4 is not the share of cabin mass in the total elevator mass and is not obtained by dividing 1400 by 1000.

After finishing, the empty cabin has a mass of 1200 kg. With the same W and Q, we get q = (1400 − 1200) / 1000 = 0.2. The established conditions of the example do not meet the required q = 0.4. In the calculation record, not only the weight of the decorative material has changed: the mass ratio on which the specific positive conclusion relied has changed.

The difference is convenient to check through the balance at a given useful load of 400 kg. Before the change, the cabin with this load had a mass of 1000 + 400 = 1400 kg, matching W in the adopted model. After finishing, it has 1200 + 400 = 1600 kg. This is 200 kg more than W. Equality now occurs at a useful load of 200 kg, which is consistent with q = 0.2.

The general role of the counterweight and the relationship between its mass and the cabin mass and part of the nominal load is explained by the primary material TK Elevator on counterweights. The typical fractions mentioned there do not assign a mandatory value to our elevator. The value 0.4 in the article is taken precisely from the conditional relevant project.

Why the "1000 kg" label does not close the question

Q describes the nominal useful load, and P — the own permanent mass of the cabin. Preserving one parameter does not preserve the other. The added 200 kg do not become passengers that can simply be subtracted from the actual trip and considered corrected.

Also, without basis, one cannot declare a new capacity of 800 kg. This would mean replacing a separate original condition and affecting other requirements. Even purely arithmetically, at P = 1200, W = 1400 and Q = 800, q = 0.25, not the required 0.4. Arbitrary reduction of the figure on the label does not restore the calculation under consideration.

There is also the reverse error: if the 200 kg were already included in the original 1000 kg, re-adding would distort the result. Therefore, in our example, it is directly established that the finishing was added on top of the originally accounted composition. A single supplier invoice without matching the configuration does not by itself prove a change in P.

What conclusion to pass along with the remark

"The calculation q = 0.4 relates to P = 1000 kg. The actually handed-over configuration contains an additional 200 kg of permanent finishing; P = 1200 kg, Q = 1000 kg and W = 1400 kg. In the adopted relevant model, q = 0.2. The old calculation does not confirm the established design condition for the current configuration."

This does not prescribe a method of revision. The mass difference is not a permission to independently change the counterweight: fastenings, loads, traction and other conditions require relevant consideration. Having a complete passport and act also does not turn the old baseline mass into a current one. An substantiated decision is needed specifically for the handed-over composition, preserving the history of the change.

If the new elevator kit was prepared before the heavy finishing, submit the relevant calculation and confirmed change in cabin composition to NPI "Nedra" to formulate a specific remark on its applicability.
